data.why: All data (isolate/gene/island tables, pangenome clusters, structures, antibiograms) is baked into the shipped HTML/JSON files under Citrobacter_freundii/Dashboard/; there is nothing to upload or synthesize.

goals: find where a given resistance gene (e.g. blaKPC) sits in the genome and what mobile-element genes travel with it across isolates
compare the gene order of a resistance island across many isolates to see if it is the same architecture everywhere
look up a gene family's predicted 3D protein structure, per-lineage residue variation, and best structural matches in PDB/AlphaFold
check whether measured lab susceptibility (antibiogram) for an isolate agrees with its resistance genotype
survey how islands and architecture types are distributed across species and lineages
search the pangenome by product name, Pfam domain, antibiotic class or subclass to find clusters of interest

review.summary: The tree states the dashboard's purpose almost exactly as the README does: where resistance genes sit, what travels with them, how the proteins vary and look, and whether the lab agrees. Its phases, tasks and 11 features are well cut and match the screens. It needs small fixes before filing: add tasks for co-occurrence, lineage and point-mutation, tidy a few click-level or misleading action labels, add a caveat to t5's filter claim, and update the check status of t12, t15 and t16.
